newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says welcomes Thai talks with IMF.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says welcomes Thai talks with IMF.

text.p: Japan welcomes Thailand's moves to start discussions with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on how to help overcome problems in the Thai economy, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.
Mitsuzuka told a news conference he had just heard that Thailand had started talks with the IMF on an economic coordination programme. "I welcome this," he said.
This would be the first step in an important action in proceeding with an overall economic package for Thailand, he said.
"I expect Thailand to be on a continued growth path and to recover trust from the financial markets as it moves toward reaching an agreement on such a programme," Mitsuzuka said.

Asked whether Japan would consider loans to Thailand such as from the Export-Import Bank of Japan, Mitsuzuka said that in principle the Japanese government would cooperate with the IMF. "Should there be a new request from Thailand we would consider it seriously," he said.

When the Thai finance minister and central bank governor visited Japan earlier this month they did not make any request for financial support from the Japanese government. But the two countries agreed to cooperate in currency markets, including joint intervention to support the baht.
